chunks: We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with us was an owner of wealth, and they mentioned the zakat, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The zakat is not something by which its payer is praised, and it is merely an outward thing — he has only preserved his blood by it and is called a Muslim by it, and had he not paid it, his salat would not have been accepted. And verily upon you, regarding your wealth, is other than the zakat.'

So I said, 'May Allah set things right for you! And what is upon us regarding our wealth, other than the zakat?' So he said: 'Glory be to Allah! Do you not hear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying in His Book: And those in whose wealth there is a known right — for the one who asks and for the deprived?' I said, 'What is this known right that is upon us?' He said: 'It is something which a man does with his wealth — he gives it during the day, or during the week, or during the month, little or much — except that he is persistent in it.'

And the words of the Mighty and Majestic: And they withhold the necessities of life. It is the loan which he extends, and the good deed which he performs, and the household chattels which he lends, and among these is the zakat. So I said to him: 'We have neighbors who, when we lend them household chattels, they break them and damage them. Is there blame upon us if we withhold from them?' So he said: 'No, there is no blame upon you if you withhold from them when they are like that.'

He said: I said to him: '(What about the verse) And they give food out of love for Him to the poor, the orphan, and the captive?' He said: 'That is not from the zakat.' I said: 'The words of the Mighty and Majestic: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly?' He said: 'Not from the zakat.' He said: So I said: 'The words of the Mighty and Majestic: If you give alms openly, it is good, and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you?' He said: 'Not from the zakat, and your helping your relatives is not from the zakat.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory annual alms-tax on wealth; the Imam emphasizes it is a minimum floor, not the ceiling of financial duty
key_terms.الْقَرْض: Loan — an interest-free loan given as an act of mutual aid and social solidarity
key_terms.الْمَاعُون: Ma'un — necessities of life, small acts of kindness and mutual aid; interpreted here as loans, good deeds, and lending household items
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: Ma'ruf — recognized goodness, good deeds done by convention of the community
key_terms.حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ: Known right — a recognized ongoing charitable obligation beyond zakat, referenced in Quran 70:24

ai.seo_question: What obligations beyond zakat does Islam require of wealthy Muslims according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this legal dialogue, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) speaks with Abu Basir, a close companion, in the presence of wealthy men who had raised the topic of zakat. The Imam distinguishes zakat — which is merely a minimum public obligation that preserves one's legal status as a Muslim — from the broader and more virtuous financial duties incumbent on the faithful. He references Quran 70:24-25 to establish a 'known right' beyond zakat: a regular, ongoing voluntary contribution proportional to one's means. He further expands the concept of ma'un (necessities/small kindnesses) from Quran 107:7 to include loans, good deeds, and lending household items. The Imam rules that withholding loans from those who damage property is permissible, and clarifies that several Quranic charity commands (76:8, 2:274, 2:271) and maintaining family ties are all separate from the obligatory zakat.
